name: Radial Return
invitation: A wall stands beyond two descending shelves. Send a line outward, then watch which surfaces it chooses on the way back.
physicalQuestion: Can a simple upper reflection produce an understandable inward journey across lower top surfaces, with a real choice to catch or skip a shelf?
nearbySensitivity: The proposed skip is tested at yaw and elevation plus or minus 0.5 degrees, power plus or minus one percentage point, and origin plus or minus 0.5 m. The all-three top descent has a narrower power neighborhood. The evidence appendix separates top contacts from edge contacts and repeated bounces.
validationEvidence: Actual Havok through the unchanged Worldcraft runtime at 120 Hz. Contact callbacks, normals, incoming and outgoing velocities, free-flight intervals, first-ground terminals, control detents, no-wall and wall-only ablations, Stone Circle, repeated loads, exact replay and disposal are reproduced in docs/experiments/horizons/return/reproduce.mjs. NullEngine does not establish rendered usability or enjoyment.

limitations.concept: An upper reflection and separated lower receiving tops
limitations.missing: This is a three-piece physical study, not amphitheater architecture. The two shelves are existing plates with visible height guides.
limitations.extension: No physical extension is needed for this relationship. A future architectural arrangement should retain comparable separation and genuine top contacts.

limitations.concept: The player can follow a return and choose whether to catch a shelf
limitations.missing: Rendered desktop and phone camera evidence and owner play are separate from these headless physical results.
limitations.extension: Review actual full-flight visibility before treating this as an owner-ready spatial experience.
